correctness.rationale: The Fourier series is absolutely uniformly convergent, and the exact quadratic form splits into 2k Jacobi chains. The single enhanced-bond adjacency has norm J+J^{-1}, certified by an explicit positive square-summable eigenvector and a ground-state sum-of-squares identity. The dominant defect has strength r^{-k}, giving the universal sharp threshold. Signed 2k-gon Fourier summation is negative beyond that threshold, and at equality all null vectors are proportional to the polygon measure by the simple critical eigenspace and Fourier uniqueness. The standalone CHECKER.py passed 198 finite tests including an exact rational 4-gon. Computation supplements rather than proves the universal lemma.

value.rationale: The circle Poisson kernel has a natural geometric Fourier spectrum, while cosine of k(x+y) is the minimal nonstationary angular perturbation. Determining the entire admissible interval for every r and k yields the exact nonstationarity scale 2r^k/(1+r^{2k}), including high-order exponential suppression, and classifies the unique critical regular 2k-gon and its one-dimensional alternating Gram singularity. These are structural and data-interpolation facts, not an arbitrary computed parameter slice.
